# TLS certificate verification disabled (Go)

`qualor:go/tls-verification-disabled` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-295](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/295.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A07:2025 Authentication Failures](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A07_2025-Authentication_Failures/), [A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A07_2021-Identification_and_Authentication_Failures/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
`tls.Config` values with `InsecureSkipVerify: true`, written in a literal or assigned later
(`cfg.InsecureSkipVerify = true`), including through a constant, unless the same config also sets
`VerifyConnection` to check the certificates itself. A callback that only returns `nil` checks
nothing, so it does not count: written in place, held in a variable, or declared as a function of
the same file.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
With `InsecureSkipVerify` the TLS client accepts any certificate for any host name. The
connection is still encrypted, but to whoever answers: anyone on the network path (a public Wi-Fi,
a compromised router, a proxy) can pose as the server, read the traffic and change it, including
credentials and tokens sent over it.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** certificate checks are switched off to talk to a server with a private CA.

```go
package client

import (
	"crypto/tls"
	"net/http"
)

func NewClient() *http.Client {
	return &http.Client{
		Transport: &http.Transport{
			TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true},
		},
	}
}
```

**Compliant:** the private CA is trusted through `RootCAs`, and verification stays on.

```go
package client

import (
	"crypto/tls"
	"crypto/x509"
	"net/http"
	"os"
)

func NewClient() (*http.Client, error) {
	pem, err := os.ReadFile("/etc/myapp/ca.pem")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	pool := x509.NewCertPool()
	pool.AppendCertsFromPEM(pem)
	return &http.Client{
		Transport: &http.Transport{
			TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{RootCAs: pool},
		},
	}, nil
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Remove `InsecureSkipVerify: true`; the default verifies the certificate chain and the host name.
- To trust a private or self-signed CA, add it to an `x509.CertPool` and set `RootCAs`.
- If you must check certificates yourself (pinning, say), keep that check in `VerifyConnection`,
  as the `crypto/tls` documentation describes, rather than dropping verification.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- `crypto/tls`
- `net/http`

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A config returned by a function call and changed afterwards
  (`cfg := makeConfig(); cfg.InsecureSkipVerify = true`) is not recognised as a `tls.Config`.
- A local variable set to `true` (`skip := true` and then `InsecureSkipVerify: skip`) is not
  followed; package and function constants are.
- An empty callback is recognised by its variable or function name: a variable that first held
  an empty callback and later a real check is still reported, and an empty method used as the
  callback (`VerifyConnection: v.Check`) is not recognised.
<!-- end: known-limits -->
